text:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — I'm sketching a new synthetic traffic generator for inference perf benchmarking. Goal: exercise kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV cache behavior under realistic but pathological patterns. Need quick feedback on distributions and what edge cases to include.

Maria Lopez: Love it. We should cover: steady QPS ramps, short 1-5s microbursts, and cache-warm/cold transitions. Also a way to pin token-length distributions to prod-derived histograms.

TJ Patel: For long-tail shaping I recommend mixing Pareto (alpha=1.2) for heavy tail with a lognormal for the body. That creates realistic p99/p999 spikes but keeps median sane. Also add recurring spikes every N minutes to test scheduler recovery.

Jin Park: Important: kernel-selection depends on seq-len and batch-size distributions. If we don't preserve token-length vs arrival correlation you'll get different kernel picks and the apples-to-apples comparison breaks. We should allow replaying (seq_len, prefix_tokens) pairs captured from prod.

Alex Kim: Agreed. Draft workload spec (minimal) — this will be the canonical input to the generator: 
```json
{
  "name": "edgecase-run-01",
  "qps_schedule": [
    {"from_s": 0, "to_s": 120, "qps": 50},
    {"from_s": 120, "to_s": 180, "qps": 400},
    {"from_s": 180, "to_s": 3600, "qps": 80}
  ],
  "burst_pattern": {"type": "poisson_spike", "avg_spikes_per_min": 2, "spike_duration_s": [0.5, 3], "spike_multiplier": 5},
  "token_length_source": "path/to/histogram.json", 
  "kv_cache": {"warm_ratio": 0.6, "invalidation_interval_s": 90, "prefetch_prefix_prob": 0.2},
  "batching": {"max_window_ms": 12, "preferred_batch_size": 8, "max_batch_size": 32}
}
```

Maria Lopez: That covers the big knobs. A few additions: 1) support "replay_pairs": true to force exact (seq_len, prefix) pairs; 2) an option to randomize client arrival jitter to avoid perfect sync.

TJ Patel: Also add a "kernel-disable-list" so we can force the runtime to skip specific kernels/modes to test fallback paths (e.g., disable fused-attn or int8 path). Helps isolate regressions.

Oliver Chen: Metrics we must collect per-request: chosen_kernel, batch_size_at_dispatch, queue_delay_ms, kv_hit, tokens_generated, p50/p90/p99 latency. Plus system counters: GPU util, SM occupancy, memcpy times, and perf tracing for NVTX/torch/cublas.

perf-bot: sample-command: `./loadgen --spec edgecase-run-01.json --clients 40 --trace nsys --outdir /tmp/edge01` (will produce per-request CSV + NVPROF/NSYS traces) :gear:

Jin Park: For apples-to-apples comparisons: lock model binary + quantization config, fix seed for kernel selection heuristics where possible, run multiple iterations and compare kernel-selection histograms instead of just avg latency. If kernel distribution differs, it's not an apples-to-apples run.

Alex Kim: On KV cache: we need specific tests for thrash vs stable warm cache. Two scenarios: (A) hot keys: clients reuse prefixes with high locality (expected high hit ratio). (B) churn: synthetic users cycle through many unique prefixes to force low hit ratio. Both should be in the same workload spec.

Maria Lopez: Good. Also include an "invalidation_pattern": {"type": "rolling", "window_s": 300, "fraction": 0.25} so we can simulate partial cache churn.

TJ Patel: Small note on batching heuristics: instrument batch-window vs chosen batch-size distribution. We want to compute E[batch_size | seq_len_bucket] so we can see if short sequences are starving long ones.

Alex Kim: Implementation plan: 1) extend loadgen to accept replay_pairs and histogram-driven token lengths; 2) add burst engine with configurable distributions (pareto, lognormal, poisson_spike); 3) hook in a scheduler toggle to force kernel-disable-list; 4) emit detailed per-request CSV.

Oliver Chen: Testing matrix idea: run baseline (current runtime) vs candidate (new kernel/heuristic) with identical spec, then compare: kernel_histogram.diff, batch_size_cdf.diff, kv_hit_rate.diff, p99_latency.diff. Produce a single HTML report highlighting regressions >5%.

Jin Park: For profiling: capture wall-time per op + NVTX ranges. Use `nsys profile --output=...` and also lightweight counters exported every 1s. We should have a small parser that maps NVTX ranges back to chosen_kernel labels.

Alex Kim: Action items: Maria — add token-length hist exporter from prod logs (low-priority scrub). TJ — implement spike/pareto generator. Jin — design replay_pairs format. Oliver — sketch the HTML comparison report. I'll prototype the spec parser and baseline runner.

Maria Lopez: I'll start a tiny prod-hist export script and post sample histogram by EOD.

TJ Patel: I'll open a draft PR for the generator code and include synthetic seed files.

perf-bot: created run 1763504500-edgecase-run-01 (status: queued)

Alex Kim: Thanks all. If we can get the first reproducible run this week we can start stressing kernel selection logic and look for subtle perf regressions.

Maria Lopez: Ping me once the CSV format is stable — I can wire it into the console dashboards. :thumbsup:

TJ Patel: One more thought — include an option to deliberately misreport client RTT to test routing fallback paths (helps test region and tiered routing).

Alex Kim: Nice, add that to the spec as `client_rtt_bias_ms`. OK closing thread for now. We'll iterate in the PR.
